deep.reconstruction:
Right half (main text). Grothendieck states and proves a recognition criterion for pushouts.

Setup: a commutative square with
- i : X ↪ Y,
- p : X → Z,
- p' : Y → S,
- i' : Z ↪ S.

Hypotheses:
- (d) S = Im i' ∪ Im p', i.e. Z ⊔ Y → S is an effective epimorphism.
- (a) i' is a monomorphism.
- (b) The square is cartesian, i.e. X = p'^{-1}(Z).
- (c) Y ×_S Y = Δ_Y ∪ (X ×_Z X). The equivalence relation induced on Y is the diagonal plus the identifications coming from p.

Conclusion: S ≅ Y ⊔_X Z.

Proof sketch on the page:
- Compute the kernel pair of Z ⊔ Y → S by distributing. By (a), Z ×_S Z = Z. By (b), Z ×_S Y = Y ×_S Z = X. So (Z⊔Y) ×_S (Z⊔Y) = Z ⊔ X ⊔ X ⊔ (Y ×_S Y).
- By (c), the last summand is covered by (X ×_Z X) ⊔ Δ_Y. This gives a presentation Z ⊔ X ⊔ X ⊔ [(X ×_Z X) ⊔ Δ_Y] ⇉ Z ⊔ Y → S.
- By (d), S is the coequalizer of the kernel pair. The coequalizer is unchanged if the kernel pair is replaced by an epimorphic cover.
- Hence a map (f,g) : Z ⊔ Y → T factors (dashed arrow S ⇢ T) exactly when f∘p = g∘i on X. Agreement on X ×_Z X and on Δ_Y is then automatic.
- So S is the pushout.

The two small figures illustrate typical gluings:
- a rectangle split into two squares (two cells glued along an edge);
- a bow-tie (two triangles glued at a vertex, a wedge).

Context. This sits in the 'topologie modérée' notes. The previous page sets up an axiomatic class M of subsets of cubes I^n, stable under simplicial maps, triangulable, etc. The next page tries to realize the collapse Y ⊔_X e (Z = point) concretely inside a cube. It uses maps of the form (x,y) ↦ (x,xy) built from functions φ vanishing on X. It then checks condition (c) for Y' ×_S Y', and notes a '≠' (a failure or subtlety).

So this page supplies the categorical criterion needed to verify that an explicitly constructed subset of I^n is the gluing (quotient) of tame spaces along a closed subspace. That is one of the key closure properties Grothendieck later demanded of a tame topology (Esquisse d'un programme §5).

Left half (rotated, blue ink, apparently a separate jotting). For a vector bundle E on S it shows:
- the Grassmannian bundle Grass_n(E), a correspondence Grass_n(E) ← Σ_{n,σ}(E) → D_σ(E), and a flag bundle Drap(N);
- the standard presentation H*(Grass) = H*(S)[c_i(M), c_j(N)] / (c(M)·c(N) = c(E)), with M, N the tautological sub- and quotient bundles;
- a splitting-principle form ∏_{1≤i≤r}(1+ξ_i)·Σ_j c_j(N) = Σ_k c_k(E).

This looks like a resolution of a Schubert or degeneracy locus D_σ(E) via an incidence variety Σ_{n,σ}(E). It is standard Grothendieck-style Chern class calculus.
errors: (c) should be read as a union of subobjects (∨), i.e. Δ_Y ⊔ X×_Z X → Y×_S Y is an epimorphism. In the displayed presentation it is used as a disjoint sum covering the kernel pair, which is fine for computing the coequalizer but is not an equality.

The argument implicitly needs a regular or coherent ambient category: effective epis and unions stable under pullback, and coproducts disjoint and universal so that the kernel pair distributes. For the tame category M under construction this is exactly what remains to be checked. The next page shows Grothendieck finding a discrepancy ('≠') when testing (c) on an explicit model.
Left half: the relation c(M)c(N)=c(E) should be read as an ideal generated by the difference. The upper summation bound 'N' is probably n = rk E. 'ξ_1 – ξ_m' is probably ξ_1,…,ξ_r.

ideas.what: Criterion: a commutative square with i' mono, cartesian, jointly effectively epimorphic, and with Y×_S Y = Δ_Y ∪ X×_Z X is a pushout
ideas.modern_name: Recognition of pushouts along monomorphisms in a regular/extensive category (gluing / adhesive-type van Kampen condition, via descent along effective epimorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of effective-epimorphism/descent theory (SGA3 Exp. IV, SGA4); adhesive categories formalized by Lack–Sobociński (2004)
ideas.where_published: Effective epimorphism/kernel-pair formalism appears in SGA3 Exp. IV and SGA4 Exp. I–II; this specific criterion not known to be printed

ideas.what: Use of the criterion to construct gluings/quotients (Y ⊔_X Z, e.g. collapsing a closed subset to a point) inside an axiomatic tame category of subsets of cubes
ideas.modern_name: Existence of definable quotients / gluing in o-minimal (tame) geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal Structures (1998), ch. 10 (definable quotients); Grothendieck's Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 as programmatic demand
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (as a desideratum, without this construction)

ideas.what: Cohomology of Grassmannian bundle as H*(S)[c(M),c(N)]/(c(M)c(N)=c(E)), correspondences Grass ← Σ_{n,σ} → D_σ, flag bundle
ideas.modern_name: Projective/Grassmann bundle formula, splitting principle, resolution of Schubert/degeneracy loci
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1958, 'La théorie des classes de Chern'); Porteous, Kempf–Laksov for degeneracy loci
ideas.where_published: Bull. SMF 1958 'La théorie des classes de Chern'; SGA6

missed.claim: In 1974, a decade before the Esquisse, Grothendieck was working out axiomatically how to realize gluings/quotients (pushouts along closed embeddings) inside a class M of 'tame' subsets of cubes. He used a categorical recognition criterion plus explicit (x,xy)-type collapsing maps, and the next page records a failure ('≠') in checking the kernel-pair condition. This axiomatic M-framework and its gluing problem were not pursued in this form. o-minimal theory later obtained definable quotients by different, model-theoretic means.
missed.quote: c) Y×_S Y = Δ_Y ∨ (X×_Z X) ⟹ S ≃ Y ⊔_X Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents an early (1974) concrete attempt at the closure-under-gluing axiom of tame topology, i.e. at an abstract characterization of o-minimal-like categories via categorical exactness. This is relevant to current categorical approaches to o-minimality and tame geometry. It is historical rather than a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The pushout criterion is standard descent/effective-epi reasoning, and the Chern class jotting is classical. The only point of interest is historical: the 1974 dating of a concrete attack on gluing in an axiomatic tame category, a decade before the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Condition c) reads 'Y ×_S Y = Δ_Y ∨ (X ×_Z X)' with Z as subscript under the second product (the transcription is correct; the 'Z' was overwritten).
'S^ε épi effectif': the mark on S is likely just a stray stroke; read 'Z ⊔ Y → S épi effectif'.

Left half: the relation reads H*(S)[c_i(M), c_j(N)] / ((Σ c_i(M))(Σ c_j(N)) − Σ c_k(E)), i.e. modulo the ideal c(M)c(N)=c(E). Read 'ξ_1 … ξ_r' and 'c_1(N) … c_d(N)'; the bound '0≤k≤N' is likely '0≤k≤n'.
Bottom diagram: the arrow to T is labelled (f,g) from Z ⊔ Y, with the dashed vertical arrow S ⇢ T.
